subject.title: fix(imessage): repair DM sender fallback before pairing

question: For non-group, not-from-me iMessage DMs where sender canonicalizes to destination_caller_id, should OpenClaw repair only when a canonical peer is recoverable, or also drop fail-closed when no peer can be recovered before access control?
rationale: That choice controls whether ambiguous local-sender payloads can reach authorization, pairing, routing, and reply delivery, so it is an identity/security-boundary policy decision beyond the mechanical normalization fix.

options.title: Repair Only Confident Canonical Peers
options.body: Require normalizeIMessageHandle comparisons and rewrite sender only when a distinct canonical peer is found, with live after-fix proof before merge.

options.title: Add Fail-Closed Guard
options.body: Repair confident peers and drop ambiguous local-sender DMs before access control when the peer cannot be recovered safely.

options.title: Pause This Branch
options.body: If the author's remaining failure is a different root cause, pause this branch and track the narrower iMessage identity issue separately.

recommendation.title: Repair Only Confident Canonical Peers
recommendation.body: Require normalizeIMessageHandle comparisons and rewrite sender only when a distinct canonical peer is found, with live after-fix proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: neeravmakwana authored the recent destination_caller_id self-chat classification fix that most directly overlaps this identity-boundary decision.
